channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Ghana rescues its government officials from Iran as Middle East violence escalates
item.description: In response to the escalation of violence in the Middle East, Ghana has implemented measures to ensure the security of its diplomatic personnel and nationals in the region.

item.title: Nigerian billionaire, Dangote turns to Chinese automaker for supply of 1,000+ CNG trucks, trailers
item.description: Nigerian industrial giant Dangote Group is accelerating its transition to cleaner, more cost‑efficient logistics with a fresh order of over 1,000 compressed natural gas (CNG)‑powered vehicles from Foton Motor, a leading Chinese commercial vehicle manufacturer.

item.title: South Africa stocks hit new highs as metals surge and rand strengthens
item.description: South African stocks show no signs of slowing their record 12-month rally, fueled by soaring metals prices and a stronger rand, according to Bank of America Corp.

item.title: Conflict in Iran spills over to Africa’s largest oil refinery as gantry prices surge
item.description: Fuel price from the Dangote Refinery, the world’s largest single-train refinery, is set to increase, following a surge in gantry price at the facility.

item.title: Top 10 African countries with the strongest soft power influence over the world in 2026
item.description: Africa is increasingly asserting its voice on the global stage, not just through economic growth or natural resources, but through soft power. Leading Africa is Egypt, ranked 40th globally with a score of 44.8, followed by South Africa at 43rd with 44.2, and Morocco at 50th with 40.6.

item.title: Robert Mugabe’s youngest son set to remain in jail a little longer
item.description: Bellarmine Mugabe, the youngest son of Zimbabwe's late president, Robert Mugabe, arrived in a Johannesburg court on Tuesday morning with his bodyguard, Tobias Tamirepi Matonhodze, to request their bail.

item.title: Africa’s richest man unveils plans to expand into steel, power, and ports
item.description: Africa’s richest man and President of the Dangote Group, Aliko Dangote, has unveiled fresh plans to expand into steel production, electricity generation, and port development.

item.title: Tunisia jails its richest businessman Marouan Mabrouk on corruption charges
item.description: Tunisia has sentenced Marouan Mabrouk, the country’s wealthiest businessman and the son-in-law of former president Zine El Abidine Ben Ali, to 20 years in prison in a corruption case.

item.title: U.S.-based AI firm Anthropic bags first multi-sector government deal in Africa despite policy pressures at home
item.description: In a striking display of strategic contrast, U.S.-based AI company Anthropic has secured a major government partnership with the Government of Rwanda even as it faces intense scrutiny and policy pressure from the United States federal government over its AI safety policies.

item.title: Ibrahim Mahama secures US$205 million to expand E&P’s Gold Fields operations
item.description: Stanbic Bank Ghana, working together with its parent institution, Standard Bank of South Africa, has completed a major financial arrangement that is set to strengthen one of Ghana’s most influential indigenous businesses.
